reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown trace Azgad's differing totals to the Babylon register predating the later Judean one, amid losses through death.

discrepancy.note: Paine notes that Nehemiah's register of returned families differs in several of its particulars from Ezra's, of which Azgad's count is one instance.

quotes.text: Nehemiah, in like manner, gives a list of the returned families, and of the number of each family. He begins as in Ezra, by saying (vii. 8): "The children of Parosh, two thousand three hundred and seventy-two;" and so on through all the families. (The list differs in several of the particulars from that of Ezra.)
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7.
